newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says Germany writes off $125 mln in debt.
newsitem.headline: Peru says Germany writes off $125 mln in debt.

text.p: Germany has agreed to write off up to $125 million in Peruvian government debt in exchange for Lima instituting certain anti-poverty and environmental programs, the government said Tuesday.

The Council of Ministers said in a statement that the concessionary debt represents 50 percent of the total rescheduled as a result of bilateral talks under a 1996 agreement with the Paris Club of creditor nations.

The write-off was announced by German Minister of Economic Cooperation and Development Klaus-Jurgen Hedrich after a meeting in Barcelona, Spain, with Peru's Economy Minister Jorge Camet and Prime Minister Alberto Pandolfi, the statement said.
It follows last week's announcement that Germany had agreed to refinance $301 million in Peruvian government obligations under a Paris Club debt reduction program.
The Economy and Finance Ministry said in a separate statement that the projects will be presented for approval to the German government over the next three months.
The Peruvian officials are in Barcelona attending the Inter-American Development Bank's (IADB) 38th annual assembly.
The ministry said Camet and Pandolfi also met with Italian and Japanese officials, as well as IADB president Enrique Iglesias and the heads of Spanish financial institutions.
